explainedBy: Thermostat battle sequence, start: the everyman points at the wall thermostat his furnace is heating toward 65 degrees.

storyboard.claim: The furnace is one balancing loop, pumping heat in toward 65 degrees.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman at his desk by the frosted window pointing at the thermostat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the two-competing-loops example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the first loop: the furnace's heat inflow toward a set goal.

explainedBy: Same stage: the second loop, drafty windows and gaps leaking heat out, and the everyman slumps, worried, beside the same thermostat.

storyboard.claim: Poor insulation and drafts leak heat out toward the winter air outside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same desk and thermostat; the everyman now slumps worried by the drafty window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Only his pose and face change: the opposing loop arrives.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the second, competing loop: heat leaving.

explainedBy: Same stage: the leak's goal is the outside air at about 20 degrees, far below the thermostat's 65.

storyboard.claim: The leak pulls toward the outside air, maybe 20 degrees; the co-host sees a hole in the logic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman and thermostat, still slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second goal number.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the 20-degree goal is carried by text.

explainedBy: Same stage: the everyman reaches to the wall and sets the thermostat to 65, the goal he believes the system will obey.

storyboard.claim: If I set the thermostat to 65, the system's goal is 65.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman reaches up to the thermostat on the wall.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: He now acts on the thermostat instead of slumping.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the act of setting the goal.

explainedBy: Same stage: confident the furnace will obey its sensor, the everyman celebrates, the belief about to be overturned.

storyboard.claim: The furnace has a sensor and its orders, so it will hit 65; not if it's freezing outside.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman celebrates beside the thermostat he just set.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face turns happy, arms up: his false confidence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the assumption being challenged.

noVisual: No icon shows 'a goal does not dictate the outcome'; the struck phrase carries the rejection.
explainedBy: Same stage: the co-host rejects his assumption that a set goal dictates the physical result; his confidence turns to surprise.

storyboard.claim: Assuming the goal you set magically dictates the physical outcome is wrong.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman, surprised, at his desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face changes from happy to surprised; the thermostat leaves.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the rejection is mostly the struck text.

noVisual: The term itself is abstract; it is named here and shown in the next beats.
explainedBy: Meadows' book introduces the term: Donella, book in hand, names the concept shifting dominance.

storyboard.claim: There is a systems concept called shifting dominance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella Meadows talking with her book in a lecture room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cuts from the example to the concept's author.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: names the concept, which the next beats show.

explainedBy: Two loops fight like two sides on a scale: the heavier, physically stronger one decides the system's behavior.

storyboard.claim: When two loops fight, the physically stronger one dictates the system's behavior.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tipped scale: two sides weighed, one heavier.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the rule Donella just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scale shows one side outweighing the other.

explainedBy: Back at the drafty desk: at 5 below with howling wind, the heat leak overpowers the furnace, and the everyman slumps, freezing, by his thermostat.

storyboard.claim: At 5 below zero with wind howling, the cooling loop becomes stronger than the furnace.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumps cold by the frosted window under the thermostat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the home stage, now in the extreme cold.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the leak winning: a cold man despite the thermostat.

explainedBy: Same stage: the cooling loop dominates, so the 65-degree goal on the thermostat is meaningless; the everyman sits defeated.

storyboard.claim: The cooling loop dominates; your 65-degree goal does not matter at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman slumped, now sad, under the same thermostat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face turns from afraid to sad: the goal has lost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Struck goal plus defeated face show the thermostat setting being overruled.

explainedBy: Same stage, result: the room's temperature drops even with the furnace running flat out; the man stays cold.

storyboard.claim: The temperature drops even with the furnace running at full tilt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same cold, sad everyman under the thermostat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds that the furnace is already maxed out.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: 'full tilt' is carried by text; the cold man shows the result.

noVisual: A question bridging two examples; no object shows it.
explainedBy: The hosts move the idea from home heating to a company: how does shifting dominance work in a corporation?

storyboard.claim: How does shifting dominance work outside HVAC, in a corporation?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host asking, in an office.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridges from the thermostat to the company example.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a transition question.

noVisual: No growth icon reads literally; the marketer's push carries it.
explainedBy: Boardroom sequence, start: the marketing lead pushes to grow the user base at all costs, the growth loop.

storyboard.claim: Marketing's goal is to grow the user base at all costs: a growth loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketing lead celebrating, pushing growth in the boardroom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the corporate version of two competing loops.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the first department and its goal.

explainedBy: Same boardroom: the corporate lawyer joins, pointing at the marketer; her goal is zero lawsuits, a risk-aversion loop against his growth.

storyboard.claim: Legal's goal is zero lawsuits: a risk-aversion balancing loop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The lawyer pointing sternly at the cheerful marketer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the opposing department beside the marketer.
storyboard.addedInformation: Two people in opposition show the two competing loops.

explainedBy: Same boardroom: while the company is young, marketing dominates; the marketer leads, smirking, breaking rules.

storyboard.claim: When the company is young, the marketing loop dominates; they break rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer in front, smirking and celebrating, the lawyer behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The marketer moves to the lead: his loop dominates.
storyboard.addedInformation: Cast order and face show who is winning.

explainedBy: Same boardroom: after they cross a line and get sued, legal gains funding and veto power; the lawyer takes the lead.

storyboard.claim: They cross a line and get sued, so legal gets more funding and veto power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The lawyer in front pointing, a law icon above, the marketer behind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The lawyer moves to the lead; the law icon appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the lawsuit flipping who holds power.

explainedBy: Same boardroom, result: dominance has shifted to risk aversion and the company stagnates; the marketer slumps.

storyboard.claim: Dominance shifts; the risk-aversion loop wins and the company stagnates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The marketer slumped and sad beside the lawyer.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The marketer's face and pose drop from triumphant to defeated.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the result of the shift.

explainedBy: Same boardroom with the bathtub: not lazy marketers; the legal drain now outflows the marketing faucet.

storyboard.claim: Not because marketers got lazy, but because the legal drain is stronger than the marketing faucet.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bathtub with faucet and drain beside the two department heads.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The bathtub appears to name the mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the company back to stock-and-flow: faucet vs drain.

noVisual: No blanket or vent in the vocabulary; the seated, sad man carries the cold.
explainedBy: Back home: the everyman sits on his couch, cold and miserable, while the heat is losing.

storyboard.claim: Sitting on my couch, shivering, staring at the vent; it's not a broken heater.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman sitting sad on the couch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns from the company to the cold home.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the person living the losing loop.

callout.text: The behavior is in the structure

explainedBy: Same couch: the thermostat appears; the heater works fine, it is just losing, so the behavior comes from the structure.

storyboard.claim: The heater is doing what it was built to do; it's just losing. The behavior is in the structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The seated everyman with the thermostat beside him.
storyboard.onScreenText: The behavior is in the structure
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thermostat appears; his face settles from sad to neutral.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the episode's key lesson on the home example.

explainedBy: A scale: balancing loops try to keep things steady, at equilibrium.

storyboard.claim: Balancing loops seek equilibrium; they try to keep things steady.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A scale weighing two sides.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the balancing loop before the contrast.
storyboard.addedInformation: The scale shows keeping things balanced.

explainedBy: Contrast with balance: a snowball rolling downhill grows from its own mass, a loop that feeds on itself.

storyboard.claim: What happens when a loop isn't seeking balance but feeds on itself?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A snowball rolling and growing as it goes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Switches from balancing to reinforcing loops.
storyboard.addedInformation: The growing snowball shows self-feeding growth.

explainedBy: Two kids on the back seat of a hot car on a really long road trip.

storyboard.claim: Remember sitting in the back seat of a hot car on a long road trip.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two kids on the back seat of a hot car on a really long road trip.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the reinforcing-loop story. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the two people who will escalate.

explainedBy: Same back seat: out of nowhere the older sibling shoves the younger one's shoulder, just a little nudge.

storyboard.claim: Out of nowhere your sibling shoves your shoulder, just a little nudge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The older sibling, smirking, grabs at the younger one, who pulls away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The sitting turns into the first shove.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the first push that starts the loop.

explainedBy: Same back seat: the shoved kid feels the jolt and anger flares before any rational thought.

storyboard.claim: You feel the jolt, and before your rational brain kicks in, the instinct flares up.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The younger sibling, now angry, pulling free of the older one's grip.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The shoved kid moves to the lead and turns angry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reaction that will feed the loop.

explainedBy: Same back seat: the shove comes back harder, then harder again; the two kids escalate into a fight.

storyboard.claim: You shove back slightly harder; they shove back really hard.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The two siblings fighting on the back seat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Struggling turns into an open fight.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows escalation: each push bigger than the last.

explainedBy: Same fight, named: this escalating shoving match is a reinforcing loop, the engine of exponential growth.

storyboard.claim: This is a reinforcing loop, the escalating shoving match, the engine of exponential growth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same sibling fight continues.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The fight is labeled as the concept.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the mechanism the fight shows.

explainedBy: The snowball growing as it rolls: the same reinforcing loop drives both exponential growth and runaway.

storyboard.claim: It is the engine of exponential growth and of runaway; it works both ways.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The snowball rolling and growing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the fight to the general engine.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reinforcing loop's growth image.

explainedBy: He points at the growing snowball: a reinforcing loop adds more the more is already there.

storyboard.claim: A reinforcing loop generates more input to a stock the more is already there.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same snowball: a reinforcing loop adds more the more is already there.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the formal definition on the stock picture. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the loop to the stock-and-flow bathtub.

noVisual: No rabbit icon; the growing snowball shows self-compounding, the callout names the rabbits.
explainedBy: Like the snowball gathering mass, more rabbits make more babies, which make even more.

storyboard.claim: The more rabbits in a field, the more baby rabbits, which make even more.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The snowball growing as it rolls.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Second example of the same loop.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: rabbits only in text; the snowball shows compounding.

explainedBy: Donella, holding her book beside a smoking factory: the industrial economy is her grand example of compounding.

storyboard.claim: It's compound interest; the industrial economy is Meadows' grand example.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donella with her book and a factory with smoking chimneys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from rabbits to the economy.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows whose example it is and what it is about.

explainedBy: Economy loop, step 1: capital (machines, factories) creates output.

storyboard.claim: Capital (machines, factories, bulldozers, server farms) creates output.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Capital -> Output.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts drawing Meadows' loop.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the first link of the chain.

explainedBy: Same chain, step 2: part of the output is invested.

storyboard.claim: You take some of that output and invest it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Capital -> Output -> Investment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds one label: Investment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reinvestment link.

explainedBy: Result: investment buys more capital, so the loop grows like a snowball gathering mass at an accelerating rate.

storyboard.claim: Investment buys more capital, more machines, more output: an economic snowball.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The snowball rolling and growing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the loop the diagram drew and names its shape.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows accelerating, self-feeding growth.

explainedBy: The everyman points at the growing snowball: if the economy is a reinforcing loop, haven't we hacked it?

storyboard.claim: If the global economy is a reinforcing loop, humanity has basically hacked the system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman pointing, surprised, at the snowball.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The skeptic reacts to the snowball.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the naive conclusion forming.

explainedBy: Same stage: he cheers the snowball; just keep reinvesting and grow rich forever (posed as a question).

storyboard.claim: We can grow infinitely rich forever; the snowball just gets bigger. What's the problem?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman celebrating beside the snowball.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face and pose turn from surprised to cheering.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows his belief that will be corrected.

explainedBy: The host points at the bathtub's drain: depreciation is the balancing loop draining the growth.

storyboard.claim: The problem is the drain: a balancing loop called depreciation fights the growth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing at a bathtub draining from the bottom.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the everyman with the bathtub.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the outflow that limits the snowball.

explainedBy: Depreciation sequence, start: a factory worker slumps beside the factory as machines wear out and break down.

storyboard.claim: Things break down: machines wear out, bulldozers break, server farms need new cooling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The factory worker slumped beside the factory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes depreciation concrete.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the capital that is wearing out.

explainedBy: Same stage: factories rust; depreciation always happens, whatever the lifetime of the capital.

storyboard.claim: Factories rust; longer-lived capital needs less replacing, but depreciation always happens.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same worker and factory, now sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face turns from worried to sad.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: rust is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: Cause -> effect: in a recession investment dries up while machines keep rusting, and the economy collapses; shifting dominance again.

storyboard.claim: If depreciation outgrows investment, as in a recession, the economy collapses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: Investment dries up -> Machines keep rusting -> Economy collapses.
storyboard.onScreenText: Investment dries up -> Machines keep rusting -> Economy collapses
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the drain into a collapse chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal chain of shifting dominance.

noVisual: No wall can be drawn against the snowball; the text carries the limit.
explainedBy: The snowball again: no physical system in a finite world grows forever; eventually it hits a solid wall.

storyboard.claim: No physical system in a finite environment can grow forever; the snowball hits a wall.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The snowball, with the limit stated in text.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the snowball to show its limit.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the wall is only in the callout.

explainedBy: An oil pump drawing energy from the ground: the economy runs on physical inputs that are finite.

storyboard.claim: The economy needs physical inputs (metals, energy, land) and they are finite.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An oil pumpjack pumping.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the snowball hits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows a physical, finite input.

explainedBy: A standing skyline: the industrial wealth explosion of skyscrapers, shipping lanes and tech valuations isn't magic.

storyboard.claim: The industrial revolution's wealth (skyscrapers, shipping lanes, tech valuations) isn't magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A city skyline.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to what the loop built.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the wealth being explained.

noVisual: The rejection itself is carried by the struck phrase.
explainedBy: Same skyline: the hosts reject the idea that it proves innate human superiority.

storyboard.claim: It's not a miracle of innate human superiority either.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same skyline with the struck phrase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second rejected explanation.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-carried rejection.

explainedBy: The factory behind the skyline: a reinforcing feedback loop running for two centuries built it; the behavior is in the structure.

storyboard.claim: It is just a reinforcing feedback loop playing out over two centuries.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A factory with smoking chimneys.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the city with its engine.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cause behind the wealth.

explainedBy: Recap of the two kinds: balancing loops reaching a goal versus reinforcing loops snowballing out of control.

storyboard.claim: We have balancing loops trying to reach a goal and reinforcing loops snowballing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Sorter: Balancing loops | Reinforcing loops.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the chapter before the turn.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the two loop families side by side.

noVisual: The flaw (delays) is only named next beat; nothing shows it yet.
explainedBy: The host, worried, warns of a fatal flaw in relying on these loops.

storyboard.claim: There is a fatal flaw in relying on these feedback loops.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host slumped, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the recap into a warning.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: a setup line for delays.
